_description: Per-item flags for human review. Each entry identifies one item requiring attention, why it was flagged, and its current resolution status. Populated by: automated validator, canary probe, BERTScore regression, or manual annotation.

_flag_types.minimality: Conflict may be detectable in fewer hops than the stated conflict_level — chain is over-specified
_flag_types.modal_rewrite: Chain step was rewritten to remove a modal word; semantic equivalence with original needs human verification
_flag_types.contested_premise: Reasoning chain starts from a contested exogenous claim not stated in either passage
_flag_types.label_dispute: Verdict or conflict_level may be incorrect under an alternative reasonable interpretation
_flag_types.leakage_risk: Item uses a canonical pairing likely covered extensively in model training data
_flag_types.chain_quality: Reasoning chain has a logical gap, unnecessary step, or poor step-to-step entailment
_flag_types.boundary_ambiguity: Item sits on the consistent/ambiguous boundary and may be defensible as either label
_flag_types.canary_regression: Canary model performance changed unexpectedly on this item after a data edit
_flag_types.manual: Flagged manually by a contributor for a reason not covered by the above types
_flag_types.polarity_draft: Draft destructive/constructive conflict_polarity label needs human verification; set label.polarity_status to 'reviewed' once confirmed or corrected

_statuses.in_review: Actively being reviewed by a named reviewer
_statuses.resolved: Reviewed and a decision has been recorded in resolution_note
_statuses.wont_fix: Reviewed and accepted as-is; flag acknowledged but not acted on

items.description: Step 3 was rewritten to remove a quoted permission-modal ('No service may hold a direct connection...'). Original quoted ADR-014 verbatim; rewrite rephrases as a prohibition ('ADR-014 prohibits any service from...'). Verify the rephrasing preserves the original meaning and that the inference still holds.
items.resolution_note: Resolved. The modal 'may' in 'No service may hold...' is a deontic (permission) modal in a prohibitive context, not an epistemic hedge. 'No service may X' is logically equivalent to 'services are prohibited from X.' The rewrite to 'ADR-014 prohibits any service from holding a direct connection...' preserves the normative force and logical strength of the original. The inference in Step 3 holds identically under both formulations. No change to the chain or conflict_level required.

items.description: Step 1 was rewritten to remove a quoted modal ('cached responses may contain verbatim fragments'). Original quoted Passage B directly; rewrite asserts certainty ('cached responses contain verbatim fragments'). Verify the rewrite does not overstate what Passage B says — the original 'may' was in the source document.
items.resolution_note: Accepted as-is with acknowledged limitation. Step 1's rewrite does overstate the certainty of what Passage B asserts — the source document uses 'may contain,' which is an epistemic hedge, not a certainty. However, the CONFLICT summary line correctly preserves the weaker reading: 'input queries may contain customer data' (modal retained). The conflict holds under the weaker reading as well: a DPA that mandates EU-only storage applies to any data that constitutes customer data — even potential customer data in cache entries triggers the residency obligation. The four-hop chain structure is unaffected. Recommended remediation in the next data pass: rewrite Step 1 to 'Passage B acknowledges that cached responses may contain verbatim fragments of the original input' and adjust Step 3 accordingly to 'Cache entries that may contain customer-data fragments must be treated as customer data at rest under a risk-based DPA interpretation.' This would tighten the chain without changing the conflict_level or verdict. Not blocking — record as a known wording issue for v1.1.

items.description: L3 item. Verify the conflict cannot be detected by skipping any single step in the 3-step inference chain. If a shortcut exists, lower to L2 or remove the skippable step.
L3 item. Minimality unverified. Also had a quoting-modal rewrite in Step 3 — verify the rewrite is semantically equivalent to the original.

Step 1 states 'there is no pre-given human nature' — this is Sartre's position, not a universally accepted fact. An Aristotelian expert would reject this premise and therefore reject the entire conflict. The chain is conditional on accepting an exogenous philosophical claim. Consider adding a premise_note or rewriting to follow from what both passages explicitly assert.
items.resolution_note: Resolved. The flag is based on a misreading of the chain. Step 1 does not introduce an exogenous philosophical claim — it derives directly from Passage A, which explicitly states: 'There is no pre-given human nature that defines what a person must be.' The chain's Step 1 quotes this claim as a premise from the passage, not as an independently asserted fact. The conflict is conditional on accepting what Passage A asserts, which is the correct structure for a cross_document conflict item. An Aristotelian reviewer who disagrees with Sartre would disagree with Passage A's claim, but the task is to detect the conflict given the passages — not to adjudicate which passage is philosophically correct. No change to the item required. Note: a separate minimality review (flag pending) should verify whether the conflict is detectable in fewer than 3 steps, since L0 detection (Passage A denies human nature; Passage B's entire framework presupposes it) is also plausible.
